purpose:
Under the Local Member Grants Scheme, each
county councillor has a specific budget which they can spend to
support the work of voluntary, community and faith sector groups in
their local community.

Monitoring of the money awarded under the Local Member Grants
Scheme is conducted by Democratic Services. This is an annual
report to the Audit, Risk and Governance Committee on the outcomes
of that monitoring activity, in line with the committee's
responsibility for oversight of the county council's governance and
risk management.

This annual report covers the 2024/25 and 2025/26 financial
years.
content:
Hannah Race, Head of
Governance, presented the Local Member Grants Scheme Annual
Report 2025/26.
 
The report summarised evidence
received from organisations for grants awarded in 2024/25 and the
first six months of 2025/26. Officers outlined the proportionate
approach taken to monitoring, recognising the voluntary nature of
many recipient organisations.
 
In response to questions, members were
informed that:
 

The reduction in
2025/26 Local Member grant awards compared with previous years
resulted in an underspend which would be redistributed in line with
scheme objectives, including support for care leavers and, subject
to Cabinet agreement, a proposed Community Fund.

Officers reassured
Members that outstanding evidence was typically recovered over time
and that councillors were notified where organisations re?applied
without providing evidence.
Members proposed
greater sharing of information on persistent non?responses to
enable councillor engagement. Officers confirmed this already
occurred where necessary.
Increasing the
£200 carry?over limit threshold to provide greater
flexibility, would require consideration through appropriate
governance channels.

 
Resolved: That
 

The Local Member
Grants Scheme Annual Report 2025/26 be noted.

The Committee
recommended the Local Member Grant Scheme end of year carry over
limited be reviewed by the Political Governance Working
Group.
topline: The Audit, Risk and Governance Committee has decided to approve the Local Member Grants Scheme Annual Report 2025/26 and recommend a review of the end of year carry over limit.

It was highlighted that the

purpose:
This report sets out for the committee the
internal audit work performed following the
26 January 2026 committee meeting, up to 08 April 2026
content:
Andrew Dalecki, Head of
Internal Audit, presented the Internal Audit Progress
Report.
 
Members were informed that the
internal audit team was now fully staffed, including the
appointment of trainee posts, which strengthened the
service’s overall capacity.
 
At the time of reporting, 56%
of the audit plan had been completed and reported, with a further
26% in progress or at draft stage, placing overall delivery at 82%.
Amendments to reporting formats were highlighted, including clearer
presentation of follow?up work to improve assurance
transparency.
 
In response to questions, members were
informed that:
 

In reference to a
red?rated action relating to SEND programme meeting records, it was
explained that while records existed, the issue related to
inconsistency and insufficient clarity of decision?making across
multiple partnership meetings, which posed risks on a programme of
such importance.

Risk maturity models,
such as the Institute of Internal Auditors five?level model, were
understood and could be applied if requested, however, recent work
had focused more on the effectiveness of mitigating actions rather
than assigning an explicit maturity level.



“Reasonable
assurance” represented a positive assurance level, indicating
that controls were generally in place and effective, though with
identifiable areas for improvement. It was confirmed that written
definitions of assurance levels would be shared with members after
the meeting.

Incomplete delivery
of internal audit work to external organisations would affect
income. Officers confirmed that while some income had been lost
where delivery was reduced, this was offset by wider benefits,
including enhanced staff experience, increased resilience, and
improved skills development across the audit team.

 
 
Resolved: That the
Internal Audit Progress Report be noted.
topline: The Audit, Risk and Governance Committee has decided to note the Internal Audit Progress Report.

content:
Andrew Dalecki, Head of
Internal Audit, presented the Internal Audit Annual Plan
2026/27.
 
It was highlighted that the
plan had been developed through review of corporate and directorate
risk registers, consultation with senior leadership teams, and
consideration of transformation programmes and emerging risks,
including local government reorganisation. The plan was described
as flexible to allow for emerging issues, in line with internal
audit standards.
 
In response to questions, members were
informed that:
 

In relation to the
potential inclusion of an audit of reactive gully cleaning within
highways following reductions in reactive activity, officers agreed
to discuss the matter with the relevant director and advised that
an audit could be considered later in the year once policy changes
had been embedded.

Dedicated audit days
had been set aside to support and provide assurance over
governance, readiness and the delivery of transformation,
particularly in managing capacity pressures arising from SEND
reform, planned savings and local government
reorganisation.

Assurance that SEND
financial sustainability would be appropriately incorporated within
audit scopes and be reflected within relevant reviews.


Resolved: That
the Internal Audit Annual Plan 2026/27be
approved.

content:
Ian Pinches, Grant Thornton UK,
presented the Audit Progress Report and Sector Update.
 
Members were advised of a
change in the audit team, with Michael Green replacing Sarah
Ironmonger for the current year. Grant Thornton confirmed their
intention to work with officers to achieve sign off of the 2025/26 accounts by the end of November
2026, ahead of the statutory backstop date of January
2027.

In response to questions, members were
informed that:
 

The changes to
accounting requirements for non?investment assets were generally
welcomed across the sector as they clarified when indexation could
be used. While some additional work would be required in
identifying appropriate indices and documenting their rationale,
this was not expected to delay the production or audit of the
accounts. From an audit perspective, the change would largely shift
the focus of testing rather than increase its scale.

In the short term,
local government reorganisation could increase workforce pressure
due to the need to support legacy authorities. However, over time,
reorganisation could increase the overall pool of experienced staff
available across successor authorities. Officers indicated this
would be monitored.

The SEND reform plan
was in development and was due to be submitted to government by 19
June 2026. It was explained that the plan was critical both to
improving outcomes for children and families and to securing the
proposed write off of a significant
proportion of the cumulative SEND deficit. Assurance was provided
that although timescales were tight, work was on track.

 
Resolved: That
the Audit Progress Report and Sector Update be noted.
